topic.title: settle ho jao
topic.claim: 'Settle ho jao' doesn't mean marriage or a house. It means become someone we can stop worrying about.
topic.moment: You list the promotion, the flat, the savings, and mummy still sighs, 'bas ab settle ho jao.'

turn.believed: Settling down means the specific checklist: marriage, house, stable job.
turn.actually: The checklist is just a proxy. What they actually want is to stop lying awake about you.

topic.because: They can't carry the worry forever and they know it. Every milestone they name is really them asking for permission to relax about you before they run out of time.
topic.payoff: 'Settle ho jao' was never about marriage or a house. It was them asking when they can finally stop worrying.

topic.villain: the arrangement that makes a parent's peace conditional on your milestones
topic.behaviour: parents keep moving the 'settle down' goalpost no matter what you achieve
topic.mechanism: the milestones are a stand-in for the real ask: permission to stop worrying about you
topic.group: adults tired of the 'settle down' pressure
topic.send_to: a friend who fights with their parents about 'settling down'
topic.why_now: wedding-season visits where the 'settle' talk restarts

ledger.text: When Indian parents say 'settle ho jao', the milestones they name (job, house, wedding) are stand-ins for their underlying worry about the child. Because the worry is what drives the request, ticking every milestone does not end it and the demand moves to the next milestone.
ledger.sentence: "Settle ho jao" was never about marriage or a flat. It means: become someone we can stop worrying about.

ledger.text: A sarkari (government) job comes with no layoffs.
ledger.sentence: A sarkari job means no layoff email.

c2.correct: Permanent, regular government employees have strong job security. Article 311 of the Constitution bars dismissal, removal or demotion without an inquiry. It is not a guarantee of no job loss. Dismissal is allowed after an inquiry, and the inquiry can be skipped after a criminal conviction, when it is impracticable, or for state security. Contract, outsourced and temporary workers in government and PSU jobs are regularly let go, for example more than 1,200 Haryana contract staff and SAIL's cut to its contract workforce. A blanket 'no layoffs' is too absolute. It holds only for regular posts, as protection from arbitrary removal.

sources.quote: no civil servant shall be dismissed or removed or reduced in rank except after an inquiry (Article 311(2)); exceptions: criminal conviction, not reasonably practicable to hold inquiry, security of the State
Haryana government ends contracts of over 1,200 employees

mechanism.broken_premise: None. Most of the post is opinion: it reads the parents' motive, uses the goalpost-moving pattern, and makes generalizations about family calls, so none of that can be proven false. The checkable claims hold in substance. Owning a house removes the landlord's power to evict you, though if you stop paying the EMI the lender can take the property under SARFAESI. That's a small caveat, not a broken premise. Indian government jobs have constitutional protection from summary dismissal under Article 311, so 'no layoff email' is a fair shorthand. There are exceptions: dismissal after a criminal conviction, cases where an inquiry isn't practical, and cases involving state security. Defence personnel aren't covered. Contract and temporary government staff have weaker protection. A startup offer can be large on paper and still carry real layoff and ESOP risk, so the parents' 'company toh theek hai na?' is a reasonable question.
mechanism.actual_mechanism: The post doesn't depend on any product, price, fee, law or market working a certain way. Its claim is about why parents keep asking, and that's an interpretation. The few concrete facts it uses are broadly accurate. Clause (2) of Article 311 bars dismissing, removing or demoting a civil servant without an inquiry and a hearing. That's the job security parents mean by 'sarkari'. An owned flat removes landlord eviction risk, though a home loan brings foreclosure risk instead. Because the security premises hold and the rest is opinion, the conclusion follows on the post's own terms.

sources.quote: Constitution of India, Art. 311(2) (text recalled from memory; neither this page nor the official text was opened to check it): 'No such person as aforesaid shall be dismissed or removed or reduced in rank except after an inquiry in which he has been informed of the charges against him and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard in respect of those charges.'

Paraphrase from search summary, not verbatim: Article 311 limits the President's or Governor's 'doctrine of pleasure' power under Article 310. It requires an inquiry before a civil servant is dismissed, with exceptions for criminal conviction, impracticability and state security.
